title: Authentication
description: Configure operator credentials and understand the difference between an access token and a public link.

sections.title: Choose an operator token
paragraphs: LOFT_TOKEN is the primary bearer token. It defaults to dev for local development; choose a random value before exposing the API remotely. All authenticated clients of this installation share its store.
sections.code:
export LOFT_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
export LOFT_SIGNING_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"

sections.title: Authenticate requests
paragraphs: Send Authorization: Bearer followed by the exact token on /v1 requests. GET /health is unauthenticated.

sections.title: Additional tokens and rotation
paragraphs: LOFT_TOKENS accepts a comma-separated list of additional tokens. These grant access to the same data, not isolated accounts. During rotation, update your clients, then remove the old token and restart the service.
Set a separate, stable LOFT_SIGNING_KEY if access-token rotation should not change the key used to validate share URLs. Changing the signing key invalidates existing signatures.

sections.title: Browser credentials
paragraphs: The self-hosted browser interface stores its operator token locally in that browser. Use it only on a web origin you control. Never put LOFT_TOKEN in a VITE_ variable, which would bundle the secret into public JavaScript.
Share recipients use a signed URL. File-request recipients use an issued request token. Neither needs your operator token.
